Course Descriptions
introductory Note
Prerequisite: For all courses in the Department of Chemical Engineering, registration in the Department or permission of the Associate Chairman (Undergraduate Studies) is a requirement.

courses.label: CHE 100
courses.title: Weeks 0.75
paras: Chemical Engineering Concepts 1 An introduction to the basic methods and principles used by engineers in the analysis and design of physical processes: units, dimensions, and measurements; mass balances; behaviour of fluids. Laboratory on visual communication is included.

courses.label: CHE 101
courses.title: Chemica! Engineering Concepts 2
paras: An extension of the topics covered in. CH E 100; energy balances; laboratory experiments illustrate the physical principles discussed.

courses.label: CHE 102
courses.title: Chemistry for Engineers
paras: Chemical principles with applications in engineering. Stoichiometric calculations, properties of gases, properties of liquids and solutions; gas phase chemical equilibrium, ionic equilibrium in aqueous solution, oxidation-reduction reactions, chemical kinetics.

courses.label: CHE 210
courses.title: Transport Processes 1 (Equilibrium State Operations)
paras: Equilibrium between phases; the equilibrium-stage concept. Cascades of Stages with and without reflux; examples of their analysis when used to separate components by distillation, extraction, absorption and leaching. Introduction to computer methods for multicomponent mixtures.

courses.label: CHE 213
courses.title: Transport Processes 2 (Fluid Mechanics)
paras: Fundamentals of fluid flow; conservation laws for mass, momentum and mechanical energy; flow of fluid in conduits; flow past immersed bodies. Description, collection and separation of particulate systems.

courses.label: CHE 220
courses.title: Applied Mathematics 1
paras: Basic concepts of probability and their relevance to engineering decisions. Statistical frequency distributions, tests of significance, correlations, curve fitting, sampling theory, applications, errors, design of experiments.

courses.label: CHE 230
courses.title: Physical Chemistry 1
paras: Introduction to physical chemistry. Ideal and real gases, the kinetic theory of gases, first law of thermodynamics, thermochemistry, heats of reaction, second law, chemical equilibria in simple systems, phase equilibria in simple systems, third taw.

courses.label: CHE 231
courses.title: Physical Chemistry 2
paras: Thermodynamics of systems of variable composition; properties of solutions, ideal solutions, colligative properties of solutions, phase equilibria in complex systems, non-ideal solutions. Surface phenomena. Chemical kinetics; empirical laws and mechanisms.
Prereq: CH £ 230

courses.label: CHE 232
courses.title: Inorganic Chemistry 1
paras: Wave mechanics, atomic structure and the periodic table, chemical bonding, structural chemistry of elements and compound, introductory transition metal chemistry, some thermodynamic aspects of inorganic chemistry.

courses.label: CHE 233
courses.title: Physical Chemistry Laboratory
paras: Experiments on viscosity of gases and liquids, chemical kinetics, absorption, homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis, thermochemistry, phase equilibria, diffusion, determination of molecular weight of polymers, training in technical report writing.

courses.label: CHE 314
courses.title: Transport Processes 3 (Heat Transter)
paras: Introduction to heat transfer, momentumheat transfer analogies and dimensional analysis, steady and transient heat conduction, convection and applications to engineering problems, radiant heat transfer and heat transfer with change of phase.
Prereq: CH E 213

courses.label: CHE 317
courses.title: Transport Processes 4 (Mass Transfer)
paras: Mass transfer. by molecular and’ turbulent motion, heat-mass transfer analogies, mass transfer models and

- application to separations such as distillation, absorption, adsorption, extraction, etc., simultaneous heat and mass transfer in gas-liquid contacting and solids drying; introduction to mass transfer with chemical reaction.
Prereq: CHE 314

courses.label: CHE 320
courses.title: Applied Mathematics 2
paras: Gamma-Beta-and error-functions; sinecosine-, exponential- and ellipticintegrats, linear differential equatians; Wronskian, Green function; initial and boundary value problems; Bessel functions; Fourier series, integrals and transforms; orthogonal functions; Laplace transforms; applications.

courses.label: CHE 321
courses.title: Process Dynamics and Control 1
paras: Block and signal flow diagrams, proportional-integral-derivative controllers, frequency response techniques, analytical and graphical Stability criteria. Introduction to modern control theory.
Prereq: MATH 216, CH E 314, CHE 320

courses.label: CHE 330
courses.title: Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics
paras: Thermodynamics of flow processes, vapour power plants, internal combustion engines, liquefaction of gases, refrigeration and evaporation, chemical equilibria in chemical reactions, thermal pollution, the energy crisis, efficient energy utilization and thermodynamics.
Prereq: CH E 231

courses.label: CHE 331
courses.title: Chemical Reaction Engineering
paras: Homogeneous reactors; batch, CSTR, tubular flow systems, ideal models, ~ tesidence time distributions in ideal reactors, temperature effects, steady states, semi-batch systems, nonideal behaviour. Heterogeneous catalysis; mass transfer effects; catalytic rate equations, fixed and fluidized bed reactors.
Prereq: CH E 231

courses.label: CHE 332
courses.title: Inorganic Chemistry 2
paras: Introductory electrochemistry; electrolysis, electrolytic conductance and transport, reversible, electrode processes, irreversible electrode processes and electrode kinetics, electrochemical measurements and their analytical applications, chemistry of corrosion.
Prereq: CH E 232

courses.label: CHE 333
courses.title: Instrumental Methods of Chemical Analysis
paras: An introduction to modern analysis including optical, electrochemical, radiochemical, chromatographic and spectroscopic methods.

courses.label: CHE 382
courses.title: Engineering Economics and Process Design 1
paras: Mathematics of finance, time value of money, taxes and depreciation, profitability, estimation of capital and production costs. Linear programming. Study of piping, valves, pumps, compressors, and fans. Materials of construction.

courses.label: CHE 410
courses.title: Chemical Engineering Laboratory
paras: Experimental applications of physical and chemical principies using pilot scale equipment, experiments illustrating major unit operations (distillation, absorption, extraction, drying, humidification). Prereq: CH E 314
: Course Descriptions Chemical Engineering

courses.label: CHE 484
courses.title: Engineering Economics and Process Design 2
paras: The business cycle and financial Statements, cost accounting, optimization. Study of pressure vessels and equipment for heat and mass transfer.

courses.label: CHE 486
courses.title: Technical Seminar
paras: Each student will be expected to prepare and deliver a seminar on material from the recent literature or industrial experience, as well as an impromptu talk on a variety of topics. This course is graded CR or NCR, and CR must be obtained as a requirement for graduation.

courses.label: CHE 501
courses.title: The Engineer as Entrepreneur
paras: A survey course covering the place of small business in Canadian manufacturing. The role of innovation in organizing a successful new business. Topics important to business startup; patents, business plans, financing new ventures, bookkeeping, marketing, government assistance, taxation, and bankruptcy.

courses.label: CHE 502
courses.title: Fundamentals of Petroleum Production
paras: Background for understanding the physical principles involved and the terminology used in petroleum production. Fundamentals of surface chemistry (capillarity), characterization of and fluid flow through porous media. Principles of production performance, water flooding and enhanced recovery techniques.

courses.label: CHE 510
courses.title: Prediction of Physico-chemicai Properties
paras: Methods of estimating physico-chemical Properties of gases and liquids in cases where experimental values are absent. Prediction is usually based on correlations of a form suggested in part by theory, with empirical constants based on experimental data.

courses.label: CHE 515
courses.title: Two-Phase Flow Operations
paras: Introductory theory of one-dimensional two-phase flow; conventions, definitions, homogeneous theory, separated flow (Lockhart-Martinelli), particulate characterization and behaviour; applications; two-phase flow in pipes, boiling and evaporation, filtration.
Chemical Engineering

courses.label: CHE 517
courses.title: Performance of Separation Processes
paras: Introduction, patterns of change and computational approaches, group methods, limited flows and stage requirements, capacity and efficiency of contacting devices, energy requirements, selection, optimal design and operation, mass transfer with chemical reaction.

courses.label: CHE 520
courses.title: Chemical Engineering Analysis
paras: Apptication of advanced mathematical
techniques to the analysis of chemical engineering processes.

courses.label: CHE 521
courses.title: Process Dynamics and Control 2
paras: Computer control, state space methods.
control of complex chemical systems. Prereq: CH E 321

courses.label: CHE 523
courses.title: Process Control Laboratory
paras: Experiments on process dynamics, control and: analog simulation of chemical processes. Time constant, step and frequency response, controller settings, cascade’ control of thermal, liquid level, and reaction systems. Prereq: CH E 321

courses.label: CHE 540
courses.title: Introduction to Polymer Science
paras: Basic definitions and polymer nomenclature, molecular weight averages and distributions, constitutional and configurational isomerism, rubber elasticity, step-growth and free radical chain growth polymerizations, emulsion polymerization.
Prereq: CH E 231, CHEM 254 or equivalent
Antireq: CHEM 353

courses.label: CHE 541
courses.title: Physical Chemistry of Polymers
paras: Polymer solutions,. molecular characterization of polymers, molecular weight distributions, morphology and crystallinity in polymers. reaction and kinetics and mechanism of addition and condensation polymerization.
Prereq: CH E 540

courses.label: CHE 543
courses.title: Polymer Laboratory
paras: Experimental studies of polymerization
and physical properties of polymers.
condensation and addition
polymerization, copolymerization.
molecular weight, extrusion rheology. Coreq: CH E 541

courses.label: CHE 550
courses.title: Introduction to Extractive Metallurgy
paras: Physical and chemical nature of ores and intermediates, introductory pyrometallurgy, hydrometallurgy and electrometaliurgy, survey of extraction processes, application of the principles of thermodynamics and kinetics to metallurgical processes.

courses.label: CHE 551
courses.title: Metallurgical Chemistry
paras: lonic equilibria, thermodynamics and kinetics of reactions in solution, bonding, stability and stereochemistry of coordination compounds and mechanisms of their reaction, introductory hydrometallurgy, corrosion and homogeneous catalysis.

courses.label: CHE 553
courses.title: Principles of High Temperature Extractive Metallurgy
paras: In-depth discussion of several processes of importance in Canada; blast-furnace smelting (iron, lead, zinc), steel making and other specialized refining processes, pyrometallurgical treatment of sulfide ores, and fused salt electrolysis. The emphasis is on the interplay of the underlying
. thermodynamic, kinetic, transport, and
process-engineering considerations.

courses.label: CHE 560
courses.title: Fermentation Operations
paras: Application of process engineering principles to the design and operation of fermentation reactors which are widely used in the pharmaceutical, food, brewing, and waste treatment industries. Aspects of mass transfer, heat transfer, mixing, and rheology with biochemical and biological constraints. Course includes some lab work.
Prereq: CH E 560 or permission of instructor

courses.label: CHE 563
courses.title: Food Processing
paras: Applications of unsteady and steady heat and/or mass transfer operations to processing natural and texturized foods. Design and analysis of sterilization, low temperature preservation, concentration, separation and purification processes. Effects of formulation, additives, and processing on organoleptic and . nutritional quality.
Prereq: CH E 560 or permission of instructor.

courses.label: CHE 570
courses.title: Air Pollution
paras: Treatment of gaseous waste products from representative Canadian industries; characterization and toxicity of filtration, scrubbing, cycloning, electrostatic precipitation, and other chemical treatment, legal, socio-political, economic and engineering aspects.

courses.label: CHE 571
courses.title: Water Pollution
paras: Treatment of waste water from metals processing industries; waste characterization, toxicity, recycling; treatment by electro-oxidation/reduction, ion exchange, solvent extraction, absorption, electrodialysis, reverse osmosis, etc.; economics, regulations, moral, legal, social and political implications.
CHE 6580 SF 6L 05 Research-Design Project 1 Individually supervised research and/or design project on any Chemical Engineering subject chosen by the student-professor group. Written report required.

courses.label: CHE 581
courses.title: Research-Design Project 2 Continuation of CH E 580 Equivalent to
paras: 2 one-term courses. A written report, meeting minimum technical report standards, and a public oral presentation will be required.

courses.label: CHE 583
courses.title: Process System Design
paras: The undergraduate curriculum is brought together to accomplish, by team effort, the basic objective of the process engineer: the design of an integrated process. A written report, meeting minimum technical report standards, and a public oral presentation will be required.

courses.label: CHE 585
courses.title: Technical Elective Project
paras: An individually supervised research or design project, based on 1 of the technical elective courses taken in the 4A term. A written report meeting minimum technical report standards, and a public oral presentation will be required.

courses.label: CHE 007
courses.title: General Awareness Seminar Informal discussions on the Chemical
paras: Engineering program.

Course Descriptions
Some courses are regularly given every other year, and are listed in their regular places. Any other courses not offered in the current academic year are listed at the end of this section..
Introductory Note

In all cases, it is the student's responsibility to determine eligibility to enter a course. It is advisable to obtain special consents in writing before registration period to avoid delays and complications.
Most 300- and 400-level courses are listed as 2 lecture hours. An additional hour may be scheduled at the discretion of the lecturer, usually for a tutorial.
COURSES CARRYING NO UNIVERSITY CREDIT

courses.label: CHEM 001
courses.title: Pre-University Chemistry
paras: The course covers the material considered essential preparation for first year chemistry courses. Included are formulae, nomenclature, stoichiometry, an introduction to thermochemistry, solution chemistry, chemical equilibria, acids, bases, oxidation-reduction reactions, kinetics and bonding. Successful completion of this course fulfills the University Admission requirements where high school chemistry is necessary. No University credit. Offered by correspondence only.

General Chemistry Seminar Required for all Chemistry students. beyond Year 1, this seminar brings together students from all years to receive information concerning the activities of the Chemistry Department and the Chernical Institute of Canada, and to hear invited speakers.

courses.label: CHEM 123
courses.title: Chemical Reactions, Equilibria and Kinetics
paras: The stoichiometry of compounds and chemical reactions; principles of equilibria, solubility and acid-base equilibria; electrochemistry; chemical kinetics. ; Prereq: Grade 13 Chemistry, Mathematics (Calculus) Coreq: (for Science students) CHEM 123L

courses.label: CHEM 124
courses.title: Organic Chemistry 1
paras: Bonding in carbon compounds. Structures, properties and nomenclature of several important classes of organic compounds. Interconversions of functional groups. Mechanisms of organic reactions.
Prereq: Grade 13 Chemistry, Mathematics (Calculus)
CHEM 123 strongly recommended

paras: Selected experiments for students taking CHEM 124.

courses.label: CHEM 212
courses.title: Structure and Bonding
paras: Classical and wave theories of the electronic structure of atoms. The periodic table. Formation and characteristics of ionic and covalent bonds. Molecular orbital and valence bond theories. courses.title: Development of Chemical Bonding and Structure

Antireq: CHEM 212

courses.title: Chemistry of Non-Transition Elements
paras: Group trends in main group chemistry. Emphasis will be placed on correlation of structure with physical properties in various groups of compounds.

courses.title: Physical Chemistry 1

courses.title: Organometallic Chemistry
paras: The synthesis, characterization and reactivity of compounds containing metal-carbon covalent bonds. Metal carbonyls and their derivatives. Olefin, acetylene, pi-arene and related complexes. The nature of the metalcarbon bond. Catalysis by transition metal organometallics.

courses.title: Biological Aspects of Inorganic Chemistry
paras: Metalloproteins and other metalcontaining biological molecules in hydrolytic enzymes; redox reactions; nitrogen fixation and oxygen transport; the role of alkali and alkaline earth metal cations.
Prereq: CHEM 312 or 316

courses.label: CHEM 420
courses.title: Analytical Chemistry
paras: Selected topics in modern analysis of inorganic materials such as rocks, ores, ceramics, metals and alloys; atomic flame spectroscopic methods, analytical X-ray techniques, methods for ultrapure materials, trace and micro determinations.
Prereq: CHEM 221 or permission of instructor

courses.label: CHEM 421
courses.title: Mass Spectral and Chromatographic Analysis
paras: Techniques and fundamental principles of combining chromatography and mass spectrometry for the identification of chemical compounds.

courses.label: CHEM 422
courses.title: Thermal and Electrical Analytical Methods
paras: Techniques and fundamental principles of thermal and electroanalytical methods.
Prereq: CHEM 221, PHYS 243 or permission of instructor

courses.label: CHEM 482
courses.title: Metabolism 2
paras: Properties and metabolism of porphyrins, purines, pyrimidines and biogenic amines. Structure-function relationships of enzymes. Control and transport mechanisms.

courses.label: CHEM 433
courses.title: Advanced Biochemistry
paras: Oxidative phosphorylation. Vision. Mevalonic acid pathways. Serine proteases. Prostaglandins. Salt balance. Respiration.

courses.label: CHEM 434
courses.title: Applied Biochemistry
paras: Chemistry and function of antibiotics: blood coagulation and related topics. Immunochemistry. Nutritional aspects of food.
Prereq: CHEM 333

courses.label: CHEM 435
courses.title: Bioorganic Mechanisms |
paras: Modern techniques of biosynthetic
studies. Enzyme reaction mechanisms. Prereq: CHEM 237 and one of 368.

courses.label: CHEM 452
courses.title: Colloids, Liquid Crystals and Bilayer Chemistry
paras: The colloidal size range, the importance of the interface, classical studies on Brownian motion, light scattering, the micelle formation of detergents in water and solubilisation. Phase diagrams of soaps and lipids and their study by X- ray diffraction and NMR. The biological membrane as an entity of colloidal size. The related spectroscopy, microscopy, etc. of lyotropic liquid crystals and bilayers.
Prereq: CHEM 255

courses.label: CHEM 453
courses.title: Polymer Properties and Polymerization
paras: Copolymerization, ionic and coordinate polymerizations, introduction to polymer reaction engineering, mechanical properties of polymers, polymer ~ mixtures. Prereq: CHEM 353 or equivalent Antireq: CH E 541

courses.label: CHEM 454
courses.title: Surface Chemistry
paras: An introduction to the physical chemistry of surfaces. Qualitative and quantitative descriptions of surfaces and interfaces and the development of relevant techniques and theories. Application to surface tension, spreading, wetting, adsorption, and other interfacial phenomena. ‘ Prereq: CHEM 358

courses.label: CHEM 455
courses.title: Electrochemistry
paras: Electrolytic conductance and transport, thermodynamics of electrolytic cells. Reversible and irreversible electrode processes, metallic corrosion. Study of selected industrial electrochemical processes.
Prereq: CHEM 254 or 356

courses.label: CHEM 456
courses.title: Catalysis
paras: An introduction to heterogeneous catalysis. Examination of the physical manifestations of catalysis and the
* development of experimental techniques
and theoretical methods for the measurement and elucidation of catalytic phenomena.
Prereq: CHEM 255

courses.label: CHEM 457
courses.title: Experimental Aspects of Polymer Science
paras: Selected experiments to illustrate polymerization, polymer properties and fabrication processes. Prereq: CHEM 353 or equivaient Antireg: CH E 543

courses.label: CHEM 458
courses.title: Quantum Chemistry
paras: The nature of electronic structure and chemical bonding in H} and other
~ simple molecules and its implications for
theories of chemical reactions. Prereq: CHEM 355

CCW 101 F 3C 05
Colossos - The Major Figures of Ancient Greece

An introductory study of the achievement of ancient Greece through some of its most prominent figures. Each year 2 of the following will be featured: Theseus: The Minoan- Mycenaean Age of Bronze; Pericles and the Rise of Democracy; Socrates, Man and Martyr; Alexander the Great and The Age of Expansion.
CCW 102 W 3C 05
Colossos - The Major Figures of Ancient Rome

An introductory study of the achievement of ancient Rome through some of its most prominent figures. Each year 2 of the following will be featured: Julius Caesar and the Collapse of the Republic; Augustus: The Empire Rises; Nero and the Corruption of Power; Hadrian and the Imperial Machine.
CCW 201 F,S 3C 05
Ancient Greek Society

A survey of the civilization of Classical Greece, featuring such topics as the individual (male and female), political institutions, art, religion, philosophy, literature, social life and leisure activities.
CCN 202 W 3C 05
Ancient Roman Society

A survey of the civilization of the Roman Republic and Empire, featuring such topics as the individual (male and female), political institutions, art, religion, philosophy, literature, social life and leisure activities.

Course Descriptions Introductory Notes
1. EARTH 121-122 is normally regarded as a prerequisite for any Major program in Earth Sciences.

2. Second, third and fourth year courses may involve field trips in the fall, All those enrolled in Honours Earth Sciences programs are required to take a two-week field camp at the end of the third year (EARTH 390). The cost will range from $50-$100 per student.
3. Regular Earth Sciences students are encouraged to seek geological employment in the summers.

courses.label: EARTH 121
courses.title: Introductory Geology 1
paras: An introduction to rocks and minerals and the processes of their formation. The structure of the earth, plate tectonics and its relationship to deformation, metamérphism and formation of magmas. Earth resources.

courses.label: EARTH 122
courses.title: Introductory Geology 2
paras: An introduction to processes that shape the earth’s landscapes. Consideration of the time concept in geology. introduction to fossils, their occurrence and uses in earth sciences. The geological history of North America.

courses.label: EARTH 221
courses.title: Geochemistry 1
paras: Origin, abundance and geochemistry of elements. Introduction to stable isotope geology and radiometric dating. Basic aqueous geochemistry. Chemical characteristics of crystalline and sedimentary rocks.
Prereq: EARTH 231 or permission of instructor
Earth Sciences

courses.label: EARTH 231
courses.title: Mineralogy
paras: Introduction to systematic mineralogy. Bases of mineral classification. Interrelationships of chemical, structural and physical properties. Occurrence of major groups of rock-forming minerals. Introduction to optical properties of minerals and the use of the petrographic microscope as a tool in identifying minerals and interpreting their genetic history.
Prereq: EARTH 121

courses.label: EARTH 232
courses.title: Petrography
paras: The study of rocks in thin section. The classification and identification of sedimentary, igneous, and metamorphic rocks.
Prereq: EARTH 231

courses.label: EARTH 235
courses.title: Stratigraphy
paras: An introduction to the nature, origin and interpretation of stratified earth materials. Emphasis on principles and approaches. Stratigraphy in earth history and economic deposits.
Prereq: EARTH 121-122

courses.label: EARTH 236
courses.title: Principles of Paleontology
paras: The principles of paleontology with particular stress on the species concept and evolution; examples will be drawn primarily from the fossil record of plants and vertebrates. Laboratory work will include projects related to lecture topics.
Prereq: EARTH 121-122

courses.label: EARTH 238
courses.title: Introductory Structural Geology
paras: Major structural features of the earth. Concepts of stress and strain, elementary rock mechanics. The deformation of earth materials, continuous and discontinuous structures. Introduction to regional tectonics. Prereq: EARTH 121-122

courses.label: EARTH 260
courses.title: Applied Geophysics 1
paras: An introduction to seismic, gravity.
electric, electromagnetic and magnetic
methods of exploration geophysics. Prereq: PHYS 111-112 or consent of
instructor

courses.label: EARTH 331
courses.title: Igneous Petrology
paras: The principles and theories of igneous rock genesis. Silicate phase equilibria in magmatic systems. Magmatic differentiation; distribution and occurrence of magma types.
Prereq: EARTH 231, 232

courses.label: EARTH 332
courses.title: Metamorphic Petrology
paras: Principles and theories of metamorphic rock genesis. Static, dynamic and polyphasal crystalloblastic growth. Processes of solid-state crystallization in metamorphic environments. Zonal and facies classifications; facies series and the place of metamorphism in global tectonics. Introduction to metasomatism.
Prereq: EARTH 232
For Honours Earth Sciences and Geological Engineering students only.

courses.label: EARTH 333
courses.title: Introductory Sedimentology
paras: The origin, transport and deposition of
_ sediments. Size analysis and
sedimentary structures. Recent sedimentary environments as a key to the interpretation of ancient sediments. Sedimentary petrology.
Prereq: EARTH 232

courses.label: EARTH 336
courses.title: Paleontology
paras: Advanced paleontology emphasizing morphology, classification, evolution, paleoecology and stratigraphic value of fossil invertebrates. Laboratory study of fossil collections.
Prereq: EARTH 236

courses.label: EARTH 342
courses.title: Geomorphology
paras: The process of landscape evolution and the classification of landforms. Geomorphic effects of glacial, fluvial, marine and slope processes. Physical and chemical weathering, soil formation. Laboratory study of topographic maps and air photo interpretation. Field trips. Antireq: GEOG 302

courses.label: EARTH 345
courses.title: Historical Geology
paras: A systematic review of the geological
history of North America from the
Precambrian to the Recent exemplified
by regional geology. Laboratory work will
include study of rocks and fossil
regional suites and geological maps. Prereq: EARTH 235

courses.label: EARTH 355
courses.title: Statistical Methods in Geology
paras: Introduction to the principles of probability and statistics and their application in the earth sciences. Evaluation of quantitative data; statistical models.
Prereq: MATH 113 and an introductory course in computer programming

courses.label: EARTH 368
courses.title: Geophysics 1
paras: introductory topics on the physics of the earth. Seismology and the earth’s interior. Thermal history of the earth. Gravity and isostasy. Origin of the continents and continental drift.
Prereq: MATH 113, PHYS 121-122 or equivalent °.
Cross-listed as PHYS 368.

courses.label: EARTH 369
courses.title: Geophysic 2
paras: The geology of the ocean kasins. Topics in physical oceanography. Physical properties of ocean water, heat budget of the world oceans. Oceanic circulation, Coriolis effects. Some idealized current regimes. Prereq: MATH 113 and PHYS 121-122 or equivalerit . Cross-listed as PHYS 369.

courses.label: EARTH 370
courses.title: Economic Geology
paras: The occurrence and geological setting of metallic, non-metallic minerals and construction materials. Energy resources. Special emphasis on Canada’s resource industries. The laboratory will involve sampling methods, ore calculation and property evaluation. Prereq: EARTH 231, 232

courses.label: EARTH 390
courses.title: Methods in Geological Mapping
paras: Ten day field camp at Whitefish Falls, held at beginning of spring term.

courses.label: EARTH 421
courses.title: Geochemistry 2
paras: The application of chemical thermodynamics to geochemical problems. Development of the 3 laws of Thermodynamics; Gibbs free energy and equilibria constants. Introduction to various topics in aqueous geachemistry — such as mineral equilibria, ion exchange and redox equilibria. Various aspects of organic geochemistry and geochemical exploration will also be treated.
Prereq: First year chemistry, EARTH 221
Restricted to fourth year and graduate students.

courses.label: EARTH 427
courses.title: Crustal Evolution
paras: An analytical critique of the plate tectonics theory. Tectonic syntheses based on the theory in the light of world geology.
Normally restricted to fourth year Earth Sciences students.

courses.label: EARTH 432
courses.title: Precambrian Geology
paras: The geology, tectonics, stratigraphy and history of the Canadian Precambrian Shield. The early evolution of the earth's crust. The Precambrian time scale and problems of geochronology. Life, climate and physical conditions in Precambrian time.

courses.label: EARTH 433
courses.title: Applied Sedimentology
paras: The source, migration and sedimentary
environment of hydrocarbons.
exploration, types of traps, extraction.
Carbonate sediments and their
diagenesis. The environmental impact
and control of recent sedimentation. Prereq: EARTH 333

courses.label: EARTH 434
courses.title: Biostratigraphy
paras: Methods of using paleontological data to solve stratigraphic problems. Faunal provinces in space and time. Effects of continental drift and climatic change on biogeography through the Phanerozoic. Prereq: EARTH 336

courses.label: EARTH 435
courses.title: Advanced Structural Geology
paras: The geometry, kinematics and dynamics of structural geology. The relationships of structures from the microscopic to the megascopic scale; statistical studies of structural elements.
Prereq: EARTH 260

courses.label: EARTH 436
courses.title: Honours Thesis
paras: (A course for Honours Earth Sciences students only.) Each student will work under the direction of a member of the Department on a short research project. The results of this will be presented in thesis form and wil! be critically examined by members of this and, where pertinent, other departments.

EARTH 4387 W 2C,3L 0.5 Rock Mechanics Review of stress and strain. Mohr's circle, strength theories, laboratory tests, classification of rocks. Rock mechanics considerations in the construction of shafts, drifts, tunnels, foundations and rock slopes. Laboratory exercises will deal with uniaxial, triaxial, flexure, hardness and tensile testing of rock. Problem sets will be assigned.
Prereq: A course in Statics and Mechanics o/ deformable materials, or consent of instructor

courses.label: EARTH 488
courses.title: Engineering Geology
paras: Review of basic concepts. in soil and rock mechanics. Field and laboratory methods used to define and characterize the properties of geological materials and their use in selected engineering geologic design and construction problems. Laboratory assignments will focus on the
_ determination of physical properties and
site assessment problems.

courses.label: EARTH 439
courses.title: Hydrogeology
paras: The location, exploitation, and conservation of groundwater. Groundwater-surface-water interactions, effect of man’s activities on ground water quality, hydrogeologic aspects of subsurface waste disposal.

courses.label: EARTH 440
courses.title: Quatemary Geology
paras: Stratigraphy and history of the Quaternary Period with emphasis on glaciation. Laboratory studies on glacial deposits. Field trios. A previous course in geomorphology is recommended. Antireq: for students majoring in Earth Sciences: GEOG 300 and GEOG 401 Not to be taken by third year students.

courses.label: EARTH 456
courses.title: Numerical Methods in Geoscience
paras: Introduction to numerical methods and their use in geology and hydrogeology. Finite differences and finite elements. © Solution of boundary value problems, mathematical modelling.
Prereq: MATH 113 and an introductory course in computer programming

courses.label: EARTH 460
courses.title: Applied Geophysics 2
paras: A detailed examination of selected topics in exploration geophysics, with an emphasis on data processing and computer modelling of geophysical responses.
Prereq: EARTH 260 and an introductory course in computer Programming

courses.label: EARTH 461
courses.title: Appiled Geophysics 3
paras: Geophysical field methods for Engineering and Hydrogeology.
Prereq: Students must be enrolled in the Geophysics Option

courses.label: EARTH 470
courses.title: Metallic Mineral Deposits
paras: The petrology and genesis of metalliferous ore deposits. The description of classic deposits; the. stability of ore minerals; ore minerals in aqueous systems. The laboratory will include instruction and practice in ore microscopy.
Prereq: EARTH 370

courses.label: EARTH 480
courses.title: Field Study
paras: Depending on the demand and the availability of an instructor, a 6 week field course may be offered in an area of unusuat geoiogical interest during the spring or summer. This course will consist of 2 weeks of classroom lectures and 1 month in the field location. Expenses are to be paid by the student.
Prereq: Consent of the instructor

courses.label: EARTH 490
courses.title: Field Trip
paras: One or more regional geology field trips normally conducted at the beginning of the Fall term. These trips will emphasize the integration of the various subdisciplines within Geology to achieve an understanding and synthesis of a geologically complex region such as the central and western Appalachians of southern Quebec. Field exercises will be part of the trip. Enrolment will .be limited to not more than 30 students per trip. Open to Honours Earth Sciences students only.

courses.label: ECON 101
courses.title: Introduction to Microeconomics
paras: An introduction to the central economic problems of society, the functioning of a mixed enterprise system, the economic role of government, the composition of and pricing of national output, pricing of productive factors, and income distribution.

courses.label: ECON 102
courses.title: Introduction to Macroeconomics
paras: Determination of national income; the banking system; government fiscal and monetary policy; international trade and finance; and current economic problems.

courses.label: ECON 201
courses.title: Microeconomic Theory
paras: Theory of consumer demand; production theory; market structure; resource pricing and allocation under perfect and imperfect competition.
Prereq: ECON 101

courses.label: ECON 202
courses.title: Macroeconomic Theory
paras: Théory of the determination of the level of national income, employment and the price level, and macroeconomic policies to affect these determinates.
Prereq: ECON 102

courses.label: ECON 211
courses.title: Mathematics of Economists
paras: Application of elementary mathematics to problems in economic theary. Topics include the graphing of functions, elementary exponential and logarithmic functions and differentiation-all developed within the context of economic theory.
Prereq: ECON 101/102
Students who have not taken Grade 13 Algebra and Calculus are strongly advised to take MATH 104.

courses.label: ECON 221
courses.title: Statistics for Economists
paras: An introduction to the underlying logic of statistical procedures most commonly employed by economists. No mathematical training beyond high school algebra is presumed. Emphasis is given to solving problems as a way of feaming statistical theory.
Prereq: ECON 101/102

Students who have taken or are taking a course of similar content in anather discipline should check with their Undergraduate Officer or the Arts Registrar's Office to determine if credit will be granted for both courses.

courses.label: ECON 231
courses.title: Introduction to International
paras: Economics
Theory of comparative advantage and
the gains from trade; tariff theory.
concepts and measurement of balance
of payments; exchange rate systems.
reform of international monetary system. Prereq: ECON 101/102

courses.label: ECON 241
courses.title: Cost-benefit Analysis and Project
paras: Evaluation : Methods for evaluating private and public projects; decision rules, efficiency conditions and methods of conducting cost-benefit analysis. Application of the technique.
Prereq: ECON 201

courses.label: ECON 263
courses.title: Economic History of Canada
paras: A study of the economic development of Canada; export stage theory, industrial structure and national policies analyzed in a Classical-Marxian framework.
Prereq: ECON 101/102

courses.label: ECON 301
courses.title: Intermediate Microeconomics
paras: Theory of modern welfare economics with some applications, the meaning and measurement of economic efficiency and equity and their relationship to economic welfare. Prereq: ECON 201, 202

courses.label: ECON 302
courses.title: Monetary Theory and Banking
paras: Monetary theory and banking in an open
economy; national policies for achieving
full employment, price stability, and
equilibrium in the balance of payments. Prereq: ECON 201, 202, 231

courses.label: ECON 303
courses.title: Economic Thought
paras: A critical survey of the development of
economic thought from the pre-
Socratics to the Post-Keynesians.
Emphasis on Classical Economics. Prereq: ECON 201, 202, 231

courses.label: ECON 311
courses.title: Introduction to Mathematical
paras: Economics
Mathematical treatment of some micro-
and macro-partial and general
equilibrium models; programming and
other techniques; simple growth models. Prereq: ECON 201, 202, 211 (or
MATH 130)

courses.label: ECON 321
courses.title: Introduction to Econometrics
paras: Introductory level course in
econometrics; includes economic model
building and testing, regression and
correlation analysis, and price indices. Prereq: ECON 221.

ECON’331 F 3C 05 International Trade and Finance An examination of theories of international trade and finance at an intermediate level. Topics include theories of trade structure (Ricardian, Heckscher-Ohlin, and product cycle), the . effects of tariffs and multinational corporation behaviour, the balance of payments, and the workings of the exchange market.
Prereq: ECON 231, 201

courses.label: ECON 333
courses.title: Interregional Economics
paras: Application of economic theory to analyses of structural characteristics, growth and development in interregional systems. Models examined include integration of regional economic analysis in view of Canadian policy, export-base, shiftshare, neo-classical, cumulative causation.
Prereq: ECON 201, 231

courses.label: ECON 335
courses.title: Economic Development
paras: The nature of the problem of economic development; theories of economic development: major policy issues in economic development.
Prereq: ECON 201, 202, 231

courses.label: ECON 341
courses.title: Public Finence
paras: Tre economic rationale of governmental fiscal activity; cost-benefit analysis; the structure and economic effects of public expenditure and revenues; the analysis of income, consumption and wealth taxes; introduction to fiscal federalism. Prereq: ECON 102, 201

courses.label: ECON 343
courses.title: Urban Economics
paras: Application of economic analysis to location decisions of firms and households; discussion of policy problems, for example, urban renewal and housing. Prereq: ECON 101 {ECON 201 is recommended).

courses.label: ECON 344
courses.title: Consumer Theory
paras: The development of economic principies for consumer analysis. The course examines market responsiveness as well as conditions causing problems for public and private consumption. It also evaluates alternative economic policies for correcting such conditions.
Prereq: ECON 201

courses.label: ECON 345
courses.title: Industrial Organization
paras: An analysis of the characteristics of industrial structure, behaviour and performance with special reference to Canada. Competition and “rationalization” policy in Canada and other selected countries.
Prereq: ECON 201

courses.label: ECON 351
courses.title: Labour Economics
paras: Wage theory, training and mobility theory; economics of information in Canadian labour markets; other investments in human capital; manpower policies.
Prereq: ECON 201

courses.label: ECON 353
courses.title: Population Economics
paras: Population objectives; demographic techniques; economic interrelationships . with fertility, mortality and migration.
- determinants and consequences of
current world population changes. Prereq: ECON 201
Course Descriptions Economics

courses.label: ECON 355
courses.title: Economics of Energy and Natural Resources
paras: An analysis of the economics of conservation, especially the adequacy of the market mechanism as an allocator of resource use over time. Issues concerning the economic behaviour of Canada’s fishery, forest, fuel and nonfuel mineral industries will be considered.
Prereq: ECON 20f
(ECON 241 is recommended.)

courses.label: ECON 363
courses.title: Contemporary Canadian Problems 1,2
paras: A “topic oriented” seminar course. The class agrees to study a Canadian problem selected from a list that includes poverty, unemployment, industrial policy, and so forth. The format assists the student in gaining analytical skill through work on the selected topics.
Prereq: ECON 201, 202

courses.label: ECON 381
courses.title: Special Topics
paras: One or more special haif courses will be offered at different times as announced by the Department.
Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: ECON 401
courses.title: Advanced Microeconomic Theory
paras: This course concentrates upon Walrasian general equilibrium analysis with special reference to Debreu’s formulation and temporary equilibrium theory; the micro-foundations of Keynesian economics and the Sraffian alternative to, and critique of, supply and demand theories.
Prereq: ECON 301

courses.label: ECON 402
courses.title: Advanced Macroeconomic Theory
paras: Classical and Keynesian models and
recent contributions; theory of economic
policy; inflation and unemployment.
modern theories of economic growth. Prereq: ECON 301, 302
ECON. 403. W 3C 05
Economic Analysis, Forecasting, and Public Polley

The course focuses on the problems of forecasting economic activity (as measured by the principal macroeconomic variables), and of designing and implementing policies to contro! those variables; topics covered include a critical review of current
- forecasting models, problems
associated with lags of the impact of policies, and so forth. Prereq: ECON 301, 302, 321
Economics

courses.label: ECON 421
courses.title: Econometrics 2
paras: Review of linear algebra and development of basic statistical inference; formulation, identification, estimation, and tests of single equation and simultaneous equation regression models of micro- and macro-economics; empirical models.

courses.label: ECON 431
courses.title: International Economic Policy
paras: Analysis of selected policy problems of open economies, such as optimum tariff and balance of payments stabilization, international capital flows, monetary and fiscal policy mix, multinational firms, international monetary reform and the new international economic order. Prereq: ECON 301, 302, 331

courses.label: ECON 441
courses.title: Economics of the Public Sector 1
paras: An overview of fiscal functions and institutions; the theory of social goods; expenditure and revenue structures; fiscal incidence.

courses.label: ECON 442
courses.title: Economics of Public Sector 2
paras: Fiscal stabilization, fiscal federalism, public pricing, international public finance, social security and other contemporary policy issues.
Prereq: ECON 441

courses.label: ECON 451
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Resource Economics
paras: Advanced analysis of selected topics in the area of energy, land, and labour resources.

courses.label: ECON 461
courses.title: Comparative Economic Systems
paras: This course concentrates upon the criteria which are relevant for comparing different economic systems, how well various forms of economic theory make comparisons, the development of capitalist and socialist economies, together with the analysis of alternative types of price system and planning. Prereq: ECON 201 and 202

ECON 463 . Political Economy of Capitalist Development A study of the main tools and models of modern political economy. Micro and macro tools and concepts are integrated in a Marxian framework based on the work of Robinson, Sraffa, Kaldor, Pasinetti, Rowthorn, Nell, Sweezy and others in what can be termed the "Classical Marxian” tradition.
Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: ECON 481
courses.title: Special Studies
paras: Research and reading courses under
the direction of individual instructors. Admission by consent of instructor.

Course Descriptions

courses.label: ELE 123
courses.title: Electrical Engineering Circuits
paras: Introduction to network variables; resistors; Kirchhoff’s laws; circuit simplification techniques; circuit analysis methods; operational amplifiers and their uses; resistor-capacitor circuits; resistor-
inductor circuits; sinusoids and phasors.
impedance and admittance; circuit functions and analysis techniques. Alternate weeks.

courses.label: ELE 126
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism
paras: Electrostatics; electric flux and potential energy; dielectrics, capacitors and capacitance; flow of electric charge and resistance; Kirchhoff's Voltage and Current Laws, magnetism; magnetic materials and circuits; Faraday’s Law and inductance.
Alternate weeks.

courses.label: ELE 205
courses.title: Advanced Calculus for Electrical
paras: Engineers 1
Fourier Series; Ordinary differential
equations; Laplace transform.
applications to linear electrical systems. Cross-listed as MATH 211.

courses.label: ELE 206
courses.title: Advanced Calculus for Electrical Engineers 2
paras: Partial differentiation, relative maxima and minima, directional derivatives, divergence and curl of vector fields with applications; multiple integrals, double and triple integrals; line and surface integrals, applications of divergence and Stokes theorems. Complex analysis: limits, analytic functions, complex line integral, Cauchy's integral formula, residues. Partial differential equations. Cross-listed as MATH 212.

courses.label: ELE 208
courses.title: Electronic Circuit Analysis
paras: This is an introductory course in electronic circuit analysis which follows the first circuits course EL E 123. The topics to be discussed are: Operational amplifier applications, diodes, rectifiers, introduction to MOS and bipolar transistors, basic amplifier circuits, frequency response, elementary treatments of feedback, filters and oscillators. The student is introduced to computer-aided analysis techniques using WATAND.
Prereq: EL E 123 or equivalent
Alternate weeks.

courses.label: ELE 222
courses.title: Digital Computers
paras: Brief introduction to switching algebra. Information representation and arithmetic in binary systems. Computer organization. Assembly language programming, basic programming techniques. Memory units, arithmetic logic units, control units, /O devices. Translation and loading. Computer case studies. Microcomputers. Prereq: GEN E 121 or equivalent Open

EL £ 224 SF 3C,1T 05 Numerical Methods Application of computers to engineering problems. Number systems, errors and error propagation. Roots of nonlinear equations. Solution of systems of linear equations. Interpolation and numerical integration. Solution of ordinary differential equations. A non-numeric algorithm (e.g., sorting). Emphasis will be placed on algorithm development and programming style.
Prereq: GEN E 121 or equivalent

courses.label: ELE 231
courses.title: Electronic Devices
paras: Review of band theory and doped semiconductors in thermal equilibrium, charge neutrality, mass action law, recombination and transport mechanisms, Boltzmann relations, derivation of p-n junction de and ac characteristics, charge storage effects. The bipolar transistor; derivation of dc and ac terminal characteristics, equivalent circuits. The Junction Field Effect transistor (JFET) and Metal Oxide Semiconductor FET, derivation af dc characteristics.
Prereq: PHYS 125 or equivalent
Alternate weeks.
Course Descriptions Electrical Engineering

courses.label: ELE 261
courses.title: Energy Systems and Components 1
paras: Comparative and historical review of energy sources and systems. Operating, security and planning principles for the electric energy generation and distribution system. Excitation and loss analysis of ac magnetic circuits. Principles, circuit modelling, and performance of transformers.
Alternate weeks.

courses.label: ELE 262
courses.title: Energy Systems and Components 2
paras: Principles of electromechanical energy conversion. Rotating machines. DC motors. Induction motors. Synchronous machines.
Prereq: El E 261
Alternate weeks.

courses.label: ELE 269
courses.title: Electrical Engineering 2
paras: Review of ac circuits. Three-phase circuits. Transformers. Industrial power networks. Principles and operating characteristics of de and ac’motors including speed control. Power conditioning for supplying mechanical drives. Interface of electro-mechanical systems with control circuits and transducers.
Alternate weeks.
For Mechanical Engineering students only.

courses.label: ELE 316
courses.title: Probability and Statistics
paras: Conditional probability and independence; Bayes’ Theorem; random variables; functions of random variables; distribution functions; applications to reliability and failure rates; marginal and conditional distributions; correlation and applications to regression and statistical testing.
Electrical Engineering

courses.label: ELE 318
courses.title: Communications Systems
paras: Orthogonality and signal representation in continuous time. Fourier spectrum, Fourier transforms and applications to communications. Convolution. Transfer functions and filters. Power spectral density. Amplitude modulation and applications to techniques such as DSB, AN, SSB, etc. Angie modulation and the spectrum of frequency modulated signals. Techniques for the generation and demodulation of FM signals. Introduction to noise and its effects in AM and FM systems. Noise figure and noise temperature.
Alternate weeks.

courses.label: ELE 323
courses.title: Digital Circuits and Systems
paras: Switching algebra. Simplification of Boolean functions. Combinational logic. MSI/LS! combinational circuits. Sequential logic. Algorithmic state machines, implementation with MSI circuits, timing considerations. Hardwired and microprogrammed controllers. Semiconductor memories. iC families.
Open.

courses.label: ELE 332
courses.title: Electronic Circuits
paras: Amplifier biasing networks, single and multi-stage small-signal amplifiers, the hybrid-pi model; high and low frequency effects; negative feedback amplifiers; oscillators; noise in electronic circuits; introduction to large signal amplifiers; introduction to digital circuits.
Alternate weeks

courses.label: ELE 342
courses.title: Electrical Networks 1
paras: Review of sinusoidal steady-state, node, and mesh analysis; the Laplace transformation and applications; transient response of second and higher order circuits.

courses.label: ELE 371
courses.title: Trariemission Lines and Basic Field
paras: Theory . Transmission lines: transmission line equations, steady state (sinusoidal) solution, terminated lines, matching and the Smith Chart. Basic Field Theory: vector calculus, electrostatic and magnetostatic fields, time-varying fields and Maxweil’s equations, plane wave propagation, polarization, reflection, refraction, applied boundary value problems.
Prereq: EL E 126 or equivalent
Alternate weeks.

courses.label: ELE 380
courses.title: Systems and Control
paras: An introduction to control. Advantages of closed-ioop feedback systems. The role of the system mathematical model. Block diagrams and signal flow graphs. The basic control system design problem, stability in control systems. Frequency response analysis techniques. Root-locus analysis Elementary lead-lag compensation. Z- transforms.
Alternate weeks.

courses.label: ELE 411
courses.title: Digital Communications
paras: Review of sampling and pulse transmission. Signal distortion, bandwidth for pulse transmission. Digital multiplexing, line coding, pulse shaping, detection and error rates. ISI and equalisation. Pulse-code modulation, Delta modulation, quantization and detection errors. Random processes: Stationary process, power spectral density, noise, low-pass and band-pass processes. Effect of noise on communication systems: noise in PCM systems, optimum threshold detection, matched filter. Carrier systems with coherent and non-coherent detection. Prereq: EL E 318, EL E 316 or by | permission of instructor

courses.label: ELE 412
courses.title: Data Communication
paras: Representation of signals, gaussian processes, optimum receiver, equivalent signal sets, non-white channel noise, maximum likelihood and minimax receiver. Information and its measure, source encoding, error-free ; communication, channel capacity. Errorcorrecting codes; linear block codes, cyclic codes, convolution codes. Prereq: EL E 411 or permission of instructor

courses.label: ELE 413
courses.title: Digital Signal Processing
paras: Discrete systems for signal processing, in particular linear filtering, are rapidly replacing analog forms. This course serves as an introduction to the analysis and design of linear, time invariant discrete systems, with both software and hardware implementations.

courses.label: ELE 426
courses.title: Software Engineering
paras: Block structured languages, actual and formai parameters, recursion, formal description, relationship to machine code. Structured programming. Data Structures, arrays, lists, stacks, associative structures. Searching and sorting. Compilers. Operating system organization, co-operating processes, process synchronization primitives. Structured software design, software testing and maintenance.
Prereq: EL E 222 or equivalent
"Project.

courses.label: ELE 427
courses.title: Digital Systems Engineering
paras: Complexity in digital systems and its control; microprogramming, multiprogramming, paging segmentation, capabilities. Hardware-software homomorphism, evolution of microprocessor architectures. Performance estimation.
Prereq: EL E 323 and either EL E 426 or CS 354 or equivalent
Open.

courses.label: ELE 428
courses.title: Computer Communications Networks
paras: Use of computer networks. Network architecture. ISO reference model. Network topology, connectivity analysis, delay analysis, local access design. Physical layer, data link layer, higher layer protocols. Routing, flow control, congestion control. Local area networks. Prereq: EL E 222, EL E 316, EL E 318

courses.label: ELE 435
courses.title: Semiconductor Devices Metal-Semiconductor junctions (Schottky
paras: barriers), heterojunctions, solar cell, light emitting diode, photodetector diode, JFETs, MESFETs, MOSFETs, integrated bipolar and MOS devices, CCDs, Power devices (SCRs, power switching transistors, PIN rectifier diodes).

courses.label: ELE 436
courses.title: Design of Integrated Circuits and
paras: Devices
Design and process details of discrete
bipolar, JFET and MOSFET devices. _
Design and implementation of digital
and analogue integrated circuits.
Process, device and circuit CAD. Project.

courses.label: ELE 437
courses.title: Integrated Electronic Systems
paras: Integrated system design, memory cells and systems; logic arrays; analog system design; application in digital signal processing; applications in data processing.
"Project.

courses.label: ELE 438
courses.title: Switching and Digital Circuits
paras: Switching characteristics of semiconductor devices, non-sinusoidal wave generation and shaping, comparators, digital integrated circuits, including ECL, TL and PL. STL, MOS, CMOS. "Project.

courses.label: ELE 439
courses.title: Analogue Electronic Circuits
paras: Analogue applications of bipolar and field-effect transistors. Analysis of operational amplifiers. IC temperature compensation and biasing. Differential, low noise and power amplifiers, receiver front and design. Modulators,’ mixers, detectors. Power supplies.
Project.

courses.label: ELE 443
courses.title: Electrical Networks 2
paras: Topics from the following: two-port descriptions of ideal active devices, including operational amplifiers; simulation of non-ideal linear active devices; formulation and solution of network equations for arbitrary linear lumped network elements; network functions and their sensitivity in the frequency domain; introduction to passive and active filters, including approximation theory and simple synthesis; time domain solutions; computer-aided analysis and design of networks; simulation of non-ideal nonlinear devices and their use. Prereq: EL E 342 or equivalent "Project.

courses.label: ELE 446
courses.title: Linear Systems
paras: Three types of linear multivariable systems are studieck
1. real time-continuous systems; 2. teal time-discrete systems; and 3. modulo-two time-discrete systems.

The unifying approach of state equations is developed and the importance of linear algebra is emphasized. Topics include: time domain analysis, transform analysis (Lapiace- and Z-transforms), stability considerations, system equivalence, system decomposition, system realization. The necessary matrix and linear-algebra theory is developed as. required.

courses.label: ELE 459
courses.title: Sound, Noise and Electroacoustics
paras: An interdisciplinary study of acoustical physics, human response to sound and audio engineering. Main topics include: the physics of sound, electroacoustical systems, human audiology, acoustical measurements, audio electronics and applications.
Every third week.

courses.label: ELE 463
courses.title: Power Electronics
paras: Characteristics and ratings of power semi-conductor devices with emphasis on the thyristor. General methods of achieving design objectives. Performance and analysis of power conversion circuits for both static and rotating loads.
Open.

courses.label: ELE 464
courses.title: High Voltage and insulation
paras: Engineering . Nature and origin of high voltage surges encountered on power systems. Travelling waves on transmission systems; insulation engineering; electrostatic fields in high voltage apparatus, insulation failure; corona; insulation testing; circuit breakers and surge protection devices; insulation coordination.
Alternate weeks.

courses.label: ELE 465
courses.title: Power Systems
paras: Introduction to system concepts; aspects of power system planning and operation, Energy sources; environmental and resource implications. Per unit and co-ordinate systems. Representation of equipment such as generators, transformers and transmission lines in system analysis. Analysis of imbalanced systems and faults. Voltage and reactive power control. Load/frequency control. Power transfer and system stability. Introduction to load flow methods. High voltage dc transmission.

courses.label: ELE 473
courses.title: Microwave Engineering Review of Maxwell’s equations,
paras: rectangular and circular waveguide, microwave circuits, scattering matrix theory, microwave filters, simple waveguide discontinuities, klystrons and magnetrons. . Every third week.
Electrical Engineering

courses.label: ELE 474
courses.title: Antenna Engineering
paras: An introduction to the theory of radiation and of antenna and propagation engineering; linear antennas, linear arrays, aperture antennas, frequency indepedent antennas, measurement theory.
Prereq: EL E 371 or equivalent
Every third week.

courses.label: ELE 475
courses.title: Guided Wave Engineering
paras: Waveguides, rectangular and circular. Surface wave structures. Fibre-optic wave theory. Fibre-optic communications system. Microstrip theory and applications.

courses.label: ELE 481
courses.title: Design of Analog and Digital Control Systems
paras: Performance specifications for design. Design of compensators for single-input, single-output systems. Performance index design. The phase plane. The describing function technique. Design of basic nonlinear-feedback control systems, Introduction to digital control systems. .
Alternate weeks.

courses.label: ELE 482
courses.title: Multivariable Control Systems
paras: Review of multi-variable state space methods with emphasis on centrol applications. Performance indices and optimal control. Continuous and discrete time state feedback control of linear systems. Systems with inaccessible states. Stability analysis.
Prereq: EL E 446, EL E 481
1Open lab.

courses.label: ELE 485
courses.title: Computer Control Applications
paras: Realization of digital controliers: digitalanalog equivalences, sampling and quantization effects, fixed-point arithmetic realizations. Real-time computer interfacing: hardware and programming considerations. Modelling and simulation of processes for control design applications. Detailed study of an — example application.
Prereq: EL E 426, EL £ 481
"Project.
Course Descriptions Electrical Engineering

courses.label: ELE 499A
courses.title: Project
paras: An engineering assignment requiring the student to demonstrate initiative and assume responsibility. The student will select a project at the end of the 3B term from an approved list prepared by the Department. A short progress report at the end of the 4A term and a full report at ‘the end of the 4B term are required.

courses.label: ELE 499B
courses.title: Project
paras: Either a continuation of EL E 499A or a separate one-term project.

GROUP ONE

Courses in this group count towards a degree as electives in any program in the University. Normally, none of them qualifies as a major credit for a General or Honours program in English (see Note 1). These courses are primarity designed to make students aware of the different functions of language in various contexts and to assist them to improve their writing.

paras: A close examination of a representative selection of works by major authors writing in English such as W.B. Yeats, Virginia Woolf, D.H. Lawrence, T.S. Eliot, and Ernest Hemingway.

courses.title: Themes of Literature >
paras: An exploration of the great variety of literature through thematic perspectives.

courses.label: ENGL 108A
courses.title: The Hero
paras: A study of human excellence in thought and action embodied in representative men and women, as seen through works of literature.

courses.label: ENGL 108E
courses.title: Women in Literature
paras: A study of the nature and role of women in British, Canadian, and American literature. Works by both men and women will be studied in which women are seen in such forms as mothers, saints, sex objects, and witches.
Also offered at St. Jerome’s College.

courses.label: ENGL 108F
courses.title: - The Rebel
paras: A study of various works of literature in which the protagonist is a rebel against existing norms. The course will examine a number of rebel types. and concepts, moral implications and final outcomes either in successful realization or in tragic defeat.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 108H
courses.title: Isolation and Alienation
paras: The study of a variety of works centering on the theme of man in crisis, the stress being on the individual at variance with his inner self, his fellow man, or his world. The course will discuss the process in which wisdom and maturity are gained as the ultimate products of suffering.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 190
courses.title: Shakespeare
paras: Designed for students in all faculties, the course examines some of Shakespeare’s comedies, history plays, and tragedies. Shakespeare’s variety and flexibility in developing characters and dramatic structures are stressed, as are significant themes.
No previous work in Shakespeare is required.

paras: This course deals with the history and techniques of the short story with emphasis upon works by such British, American and Canadian writers as Henry James, James Joyce, D.H. Lawrence, Ernest Hemingway, and Alice Munro.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

The Bible and Literature
The study of major themes, stories, myths, and characters of the Old and New Testaments of the King James Bible, and their influence on other English literature..

courses.title: The Bible and Literature 1
paras: Selections from Hebrew Scripture will be studied in relation to English literature.

courses.label: ENGL 202B
courses.title: The Bible and Literature 2
paras: The course will continue the study of the Bible, emphasizing the Christian gospels and epistles in relation to English literature.

courses.label: ENGL 205R
courses.title: The Canadian Short Story
paras: Exploration of the Canadian short story, from its beginnings-in the bush, in the north, on the land, in the small towns-through the struggles of an urbanizing society to the present. Students will be expected to work in some depth with individual authors.

courses.label: ENGL 208A
courses.title: Forms of Fantasy
paras: This course wilt deal with the history and forms of fantasy written for adults. In considering the genre, related forms like the romance, the fairy tale, the fable and the gothic horror story will be discussed. Authors such as Morris, C.S. Lewis, Tolkien, Williams, and White will be studied
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 208B
courses.title: Science Fiction
paras: Various examples drawn, for instance, from Utopian and anti-Utopian science fiction, social science fiction, “gadget” science fiction, parapsychology, and altemate worlds and beings, will be considered. Some attention will be given to the historical development of the genre.
Also offered at St. Jerome’s College.

courses.label: ENGL 208C
courses.title: Studies in Children’s Literature
paras: This course will deal with classic works of children’s literature, including fantasy written primarily for children. Selections from such authors as Kipling, Woolf, C.S. Lewis, George MacDonaid, Kenneth Grahame, and Thurber will be studied.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 208E
courses.title: Women Writers of the 20th Century
paras: A study of such major 20th century writers as Woolf, Hellman, Murdoch, McCarthy, Lessing, Laurence, Plath and Atwood. Emphasis will be on the concerns of these writers with the roles" of women, the writer’s search for new meanings, and their innovations in literary forms.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 208H
courses.title: Arthurian Legend
paras: The story of Arthur and his knights of the Round Table will be discussed as it is treated at various times in various works and genres. Such matters will be considered as the character of Arthur, the concept of Camelot, and the Fellowship of the Round Table.

courses.label: ENGL 208K
courses.title: Detective Fiction
paras: The history and characteristics of the “detective novel,” the “novel of crime,” and the “thriller.” Attention will also be given to the novel of intrigue and espionage. Such authors as Poe, Collins, Doyle, Chesterton, Hammett, Buchan, Greene, Deighton, and Le Carre will be discussed. The course includes the examination of critical approaches to the form of detective fiction.

courses.label: ENGL 209
courses.title: Writing Strategies
paras: Students practise effective writing along with the study of established models. The goal is to develop language competence to meet a variety of academic, business, and professional situations.
Prereq: Second-year standing or above -
Counts as an English Major credit as of Fal 1984.

courses.title: The Novel
paras: The novel, by its nature, constitutes an attempt to formulate and to interpret the bewildering human experience. This course undertakes an exploration of the forms that attempt can take. Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

Restoration and Eighteenth-Century Literature

Literature of the period that began as neo-classical, England’s Augustan Age paralleling that of ancient Rome, and gradually, through subtle changes, became the precursor to the Romantic movement, giving rise, along the way,.to new genres, such as comedy of manners, heroic tragedy, descriptivemeditative poetry, and the novel.

Introductory Notes
1. Students in faculties other than Environmental Studies should consult their faculty advisor regarding how term courses with 0.75 credit weight are counted for degree credit purposes.

2. There are a number of courses offered in the Faculty of Environmental Studies of an integrative nature which extend across the academic interests of the 4 units, School of Architecture, Department of Geography, . Department of Man-Environment Studies, and School of Urban and Regional Planning. The courses are of a general interest and are open to aif students. in the University. There is no Department of Environmental Studies. Students interested in this area are urged to consult the course Offerings of the 4 individual units mentioned above. These four departments/schools offer a variety of related courses allowing in-depth studies of topics covered in the Environmental Studies courses.

courses.label: ENVS 195
courses.title: Introduction to Environmental Studies
paras: Theories, methods and concepts in study of the environment. Emphasis on natural and built environment and relationships between elements of the environment. Environmental planning, management, and design discussed.

courses.label: ENVS 200
courses.title: Field Ecology
paras: Introduces the main concepts and principles of ecology; the cycling of elements; energetics and structural organization of major ecological systems; population dynamics; impact of natural resource management practices and urban and industrial development on the environment; incorporating environmental quality considerations into development activities. There are weekly field trips to study natural and disturbed ecosystems, urban and applied ecology. Prereq: Second, third and fourth year students only

courses.label: ENVS 201
courses.title: Introduction to Environmental and Planning Law ,
paras: Introduction to legal concepts generally and to environmental and planning law concepts in particular. Designed both for students who do not pian to take further in-depth legal courses and as a prerequisite for senior legal courses - ENV S 401 and ENV §S 402. Topics to be covered include Sources of Law, Nature of Legal Remedies, Common Law, Judicial Review, Administrative Agencies and the law relating to them, Planning Act, Environmental Protection and Assessment Acts, and Federal Fisheries Act.

courses.label: ENVS 252
courses.title: Media Tools for Environmental Studies
paras: instruction in basic black and white photography relating to photography’‘s role as a media tool; basic darkroom functions, camera operation, composition, photographic theory, and photo essay production. Much of the course work and projects will be done outside the classroom in field situations of environmental concem using initiative in project development. Students are expected to supply their own cameras. A limited number of cameras will be available on a rental basis.
Prereq: ENV S students; others with consent of instructor

courses.label: ENVS 253
courses.title: Media Tools for Environmental Studies - Advanced Level
paras: Builds on work performed in the basic course. Photographic colour theory and Practice, basic audio recording, editing and production, and presentation formats are investigated in workshop situations. A major project is developed using pre-research material assigned by the instructor. Students work in small groups to produce a slide-sound program of environmental concern. Prereq: ENV S 252

courses.label: ENVS 271
courses.title: Introduction to Quantitative Research Methods
paras: An introduction to scientific method; descriptive and inferential statistics; sampling design. The course emphasizes the methodological and
interpretative problems involved in using
selected quantitative methods to investigate selected environmental topics.
Prereq: Only for students in Environmental Studies

courses.label: ENVS 272
courses.title: Computer Programming in
paras: Environmental Studies The course emphasizes programming skills and applications in the context of environmental problems.
Prereq: ENV S 271

courses.label: ENVS 310
courses.title: Behavioural Studies
paras: Studies of environmental perception and of the behaviour of individuals and groups in interaction with their environment. Emphasis will be divided between an explanation of the methods of social science suitable for the study of environmental behaviour and the substantive findings from such applications.
Prereq: Second, third or fourth year students only

courses.label: ENVS 334
courses.title: Park Management
paras: Basic administrative procedures in park Management. Operational techniques are examined together with general policies of acquisition, operation and development.
Prereq: REC 210, REC 230 or equivalent
Cross-listed as REC 334..

courses.label: ENVS 360
courses.title: Environmental Studies Workshop
paras: An interdisciplinary workshop focusing upon environmental issues in a project or research format.

Prereq: Third and fourth year students in Environmental Studies; enrolment is by research team only with representatives from at least 3 units of the faculty (max. 7 people) and subject to selection of an advisor and a Satisfactory project or research proposal

ENV § 401 W 3C 05 Environmental Law An advanced, in-depth version of ENV S 201, providing an opportunity for detailed analysis of institutional factors regulating the natural environment and resources development in Ontario and Canada. How satisfactory present Statutes, court systems and boards are for improving environmental quality as weil as alternatives to these legalinstitutional approaches will be discussed.
Prereq: ENV S 201

courses.label: ENVS 402
courses.title: Planning Law
paras: An analysis of the legal basis for planning in Ontario and the practice of planning Jaw as it affects planners, municipalities, local councils, property owners and residents. The roles of planning board, municipal councils, the Ontario Municipal Board, the Ministry of Housing, provincial Cabinet and the Niagara Escarpment Commission in the planning process will be discussed. Prereq: ENV S 201

courses.label: ENVS 433
courses.title: People in Natural Areas
paras: Designing and managing for people in natural areas; behavioural research and its relevance to the design and operation of natural areas and facilities will be emphasized. Means of understanding and involving neighbouring and visiting publics and indigenous people in the design and management of natural areas will be studied.
Prereq: REC/ENV S 334
Cross-listed as REC 433.

courses.label: ENVS 434
courses.title: Advanced Park Planning and Management
paras: A study of policies, procedures, and practices relative to the management of natural resources. Emphasis is placed on an ecological systems approach to management as it relates to parks at all levels of government.
Prereq: REC/ENV S 334
Cross-listed as REC 434.

courses.label: ENVS 444
courses.title: Land Evaluation and R es Management
paras: The course wiil focus on the management of land and resources. Attitudinal, legal, and political influences will be investigated, particularly as they affect the design and implementation of planning decisions.

courses.label: ENVS 500
courses.title: Professional Development in Environmental Management
paras: Those interested in qualifying for professional status and those from other related disciplines such as civil engineering, planning, architecture, and geography may find a discussion of professional environmental management strategies useful. Prereq: Fourth year students or consent of instructor
